recipes.name: Banana Bread
instructions: Rack to the lower third; heat oven to 350°F / 177°C. Grease a 9×5 in loaf pan.
Whisk flour, baking soda, salt and cinnamon.
Mash the bananas — the mixer does this well.
Cream butter and brown sugar 3 min until light.
Add eggs one at a time, beating well between.
Beat in bananas, yogurt and vanilla.
Add the dry to the wet on low, just until combined. Fold in add-ins.
Spread into the pan; bake 60–65 min, foiling loosely halfway.
Cool 1 hr in the pan on a rack.
Turn out and cool completely before slicing.

recipes.name: Chewy Chocolate Chip Cookies
instructions: Mix the cooled melted butter with both sugars.
Beat in the egg and vanilla until smooth.
Add flour, baking soda and salt; mix by hand just until combined. Fold in chocolate.
Scoop into balls, about 1½ Tbsp each.
Chill at least 20 min — longer is better.
Heat oven to 350°F / 175°C; line a sheet.
Bake 10–11 min until the edges are golden.
Sprinkle with flaky salt; cool 5 min on the sheet.

recipes.name: Four-Flavour Sablés
instructions: Beat salt and powdered sugar into the softened butter with a spatula.
Mix in the egg yolks, then the flour.
Bring together and divide into 4 pieces, about 187 g each.
Work matcha and powdered sugar into one quarter.
Work cocoa and chocolate chips into one quarter.
Work vanilla into one quarter, with a little flour to compensate.
Work the black tea leaves into the last quarter.
Wrap each log and chill at least 3 hr.
Roll each log in granulated sugar.
Cut each log into 12; bake at 165°C / 330°F for 20 min.
Cool on the tray before moving them.

recipes.name: Green Grape Cheong (포도청)
instructions: Scrub the grapes and lemons with baking soda.
Rinse well, several times over.
Dry completely — no residual moisture.
Slice one lemon thinly; pick out the seeds.
Juice the second lemon; strain out seeds.
Halve the grapes: slice one half, mince or blend the other.
Combine everything with the sugar and mix well.
Pack into a sterilised jar.
Leave at room temperature until the sugar fully dissolves.
Move to the refrigerator once dissolved.

recipes.name: Japanese Cake Roll
instructions: Line a 9×13 in pan; heat oven to 350°F / 176°C.
Whisk yolks, sugar, salt, vanilla, oil and milk.
Sift in cake flour and baking powder; whisk smooth.
Wipe the bowl with vinegar or lemon; beat whites to frothy.
Add cream of tartar, then sugar in three additions; beat to stiff peaks.
Fold meringue into the batter in thirds, gently.
Spread in the pan, tap out big bubbles, bake 15–17 min.
Flip onto a damp towel, peel the parchment, roll from the short side.
Leave rolled in the towel until completely cool.
Whip cream, powdered sugar and vanilla to medium-stiff peaks.
Unroll, trim edges, spread cream leaving a ½ in / 1 cm border.
Roll back up without the towel, wrap tightly, chill 1 hr.

recipes.name: Karaage (Japanese Fried Chicken)
instructions: Cut thighs into 2 in / 5 cm pieces; season with salt and pepper.
Whisk ginger, garlic, soy, sake and sesame oil; mix into the chicken by hand.
Cover; marinate in the fridge 30 min.
Heat 2.5–3.8 cm of oil to 325°F / 160°C over medium-low.
Dredge flour first, then potato starch, shaking off excess each time.
First fry: 3–5 pieces at a time, 90 sec, to light golden. Rest on a rack.
Skim crumbs from the oil between batches.
Second fry at 350°F / 180°C, 45 sec, until golden and crisp.
Serve hot with lemon, Kewpie mayo and shichimi.

recipes.name: Kitsune Udon
instructions: Soak kombu in the water at least 30 min (up to half a day).
Heat slowly to just below boiling; pull the kombu out before it boils.
Add katsuobushi, return to a boil, simmer 15 sec, turn off.
Let the flakes sink 10–15 min, then strain.
Combine dashi, mirin, sugar, usukuchi soy and salt; boil, then hold at a low simmer.
Squeeze the inari age; slice scallion and narutomaki thin.
Boil udon 1 min from frozen (or per package).
Drain, shaking off every bit of water.
Divide noodles into bowls, pour over hot broth, add toppings.

recipes.name: Korean Macaroni Salad
instructions: Boil the macaroni per the package, salting the water. Drain, cool 2 min.
Toss the cucumber with ½ tsp salt; leave it to draw while you prep.
Cube the bell pepper; drain the tinned corn.
Whisk mayo, sugar, honey, lemon juice, salt, pepper and dijon.
Gently squeeze the water out of the cucumber.
Combine everything in a large bowl.
Chill at least 30 min before serving.

recipes.name: Korokke (Potato & Meat Croquettes)
instructions: Peel and quarter the potatoes; boil 15–20 min until a skewer slides in. Drain fully.
Back on low heat, shake the pot until every trace of moisture is gone.
Mash, leaving some chunks for texture.
Finely chop onion, carrot and shiitake caps.
Sauté onion in oil until soft, then add carrot and shiitake and cook until soft.
Add beef, break up, cook through; season with salt and both peppers.
Drain the meat and stir into the potatoes — leave the liquid behind.
Mix in the egg until well combined.
While still warm (not hot), form into ovals.
Chill 15–30 min. Do not skip.
Set out flour, beaten egg and panko; coat in that order.
Heat 5 cm of oil to 340–350°F / 170–180°C.
Fry in batches to golden brown — the inside is already cooked. Drain on a rack.
Serve immediately with tonkatsu sauce.

recipes.name: Matcha Cookies
instructions: Sift flour and matcha together.
Beat butter smooth, blend in the salt.
Add confectioners' sugar; beat until soft and light.
Mix in the egg yolks.
Add the flour-matcha gradually; mix until just combined.
Fold in white chocolate chips.
Halve the dough; roll each into a log 1½ in / 4 cm across, 7 in / 18 cm long.
Wrap and chill until firm, at least 2 hr.
Heat oven to 350°F / 175°C; line a sheet.
Slice ⅓ in / 7 mm rounds, space 1 in / 2.5 cm apart.
Bake ~15 min, until the edges just turn golden.
Cool 5 min on the sheet, then finish on a rack.

recipes.name: Nian Gao (New Year Cake)
instructions: Whisk glutinous rice flour, ground ginger and salt.
Snap the sugar slabs into a pan with the water; boil covered until fully dissolved.
Off heat, stir in coconut milk, oil and kansui; cool 5–10 min.
Add the hot liquid to the flour in thirds, stirring until only small lumps remain.
Pass the batter through a fine mesh strainer.
Grease a 9 in / 23 cm round pan; pour in and tap out air bubbles.
Cover with foil; set on a rack in a wok with water ½ in / 1 cm below the rack.
Steam on medium 50–60 min (45–50 for a thin pan). Top up water halfway.
Test with a chopstick: the cake should be brown and slightly translucent.
Cool on the counter overnight before slicing.
Slice ¼–½ in / 6–12 mm and pan-fry 3–4 min, flipping once, until blistered.

recipes.name: Petite Vanilla Bean Scones
instructions: Split 2 vanilla beans, scrape the seeds into the cream.
Let the vanilla cream stand 15 min.
Heat oven to 350°F / 175°C.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt together.
Cut chilled butter into the flour until it looks like crumbs.
Whisk egg into the vanilla cream; stir into the flour with a fork just until it comes together.
Press into a rectangle and roll ½–¾ in / 1.5–2 cm thick.
Trim square, cut 12 rectangles, then halve each diagonally into triangles.
Bake 18 min, pulling them just before they colour.
Cool 15 min on the sheet, then completely on a rack.
Scrape 1 vanilla bean into the milk; let it sit.
Whisk powdered sugar and a dash of salt into the vanilla milk until smooth.
Dunk each cooled scone, turning to coat; set on parchment or a rack.
Let the glaze set completely, about 1 hr.

recipes.name: Ridiculously Good Oxtail Stew
instructions: Preheat oven to 425°F / 220°C with a large roasting tray inside.
Season and oil the oxtail in the hot tray; roast ~20 min until golden and caramelised.
Chop leeks, celery and carrots into 2 cm pieces.
Sweat with picked thyme, rosemary and bay in oil, ~20 min, until soft and sweet.
Drop the oven to 325°F / 170°C. Stir cloves and flour into the veg.
Pour in tomatoes and porter, add the oxtail and its juices, cover with stock.
Bring to the boil, lid on, then oven ~5 hr until the meat falls off the bone.
Rest 10 min out of the oven.
Strip the meat from the bones with gloved hands; discard the bones.
Add Worcestershire sauce, season, serve with mash and greens.

recipes.name: Shokupan (Chopstick Chronicles — yudane)
instructions: Mix bread flour with boiling water to a paste.
Wrap and refrigerate overnight, 8–12 hr.
Room-temperature milk into the mixer bowl.
Add sugar, butter and yeast, then tear the yudane in in small pieces.
Add bread flour and salt.
Combine on speed 1, then knead on speed 5–6 for 20 min.
Round the dough, into a greased bowl, covered; rise 45–60 min at 86°F / 30°C until doubled.
Finger test: floured finger poke — the hole should stay.
Punch down, cut into 2 equal pieces, roll each.
Cover with a wet cloth; bench rest 20 min.
Roll each to 5.9×7.8 in / 15×20 cm; fold left and right to the centre, no trapped air.
Rotate 90°, roll up from one end; both into a greased tin, ends facing the centre.
Cover with a wet cloth; rise ~30 min until level with the tin.
Preheat to 365°F / 185°C.
Optional: brush the risen dough with beaten egg.
Bake 25–30 min.
Turn out onto a rack. Slice the next day.

recipes.name: Shokupan (JOC — straight dough)
instructions: Pick your water temperature from your kitchen temperature; target 79–82°F / 26–28°C final dough.
Combine water, sugar and honey; whisk in the yeast.
Mix flour, salt and milk powder in the mixer bowl; well in the centre; pour in the yeast liquid.
Speed 2, 2–3 min to a shaggy dough with no dry patches.
Speed 4, 4 min — smoothing but still bumpy.
Speed 6, 3 min until it clears the bowl.
Check dough is below 79°F / 26°C, then add cubed butter.
Speed 2, 2 min until no butter streaks remain.
Speed 6, 2–3 min until the dough clings to the hook and the bowl is clean.
Windowpane test: stretch thin — translucent, no tearing.
Speed 4, 1–2 min to relax. Dough should read 79–82°F / 26–28°C.
Slam and fold 5 times, then tension-pull into a taut ball.
Into an oiled bowl, covered; rise 45–60 min until doubled.
Finger test: the poke should stay, or spring back very slowly.
Deflate, weigh, divide into 3 equal pieces.
Shape each into a boule; drag 6 times on an unfloured surface for tension.
Cover with a damp towel; bench rest 15 min.
Grease the pan and lid with butter, corners included.
Roll each to 7×9 in / 18×23 cm, fold in thirds, roll to a taut log, pinch the seam.
Three logs seam-down in the pan, swirls facing inward, sides touching the walls.
Cover and proof ~1 hr. Flat top: 75–80% of pan height. Round top: 85–90%.
Preheat 425°F / 220°C, rack 6–7 in / 15–18 cm below the top element.
Flat top: lid on, 410°F / 210°C, 25–30 min. Round top: spritz, 385°F / 195°C, 25–30 min.
Slam the pan on the counter 1–2 times, then turn the loaf out onto a rack.
Cool completely, 2–3 hours, before slicing.

recipes.name: Shortbread Cookies
instructions: Cream the butter with the vanilla.
Add confectioners' sugar and salt; mix to combine.
Scrape down, add flour on low, scrape and mix until combined.
Shape into a rectangular brick and wrap.
Chill until firm, at least 1 hr.
Heat oven to 350°F / 177°C.
Slice ½ in / 1 cm thick; space 1 in / 2.5 cm apart on a lined sheet.
Prick a pattern on top with a fork or skewer.
Bake ~10 min, rotating the sheet halfway.
Cool on a wire rack.

recipes.name: Steamed Buns (Mantou)
instructions: Stir milk, yeast and sugar together in the mixer bowl.
Add flour, knead on speed 1 for 6 min to a smooth dough.
Cover and rest 5 min.
Roll out to a 14×10 in / 35×25 cm rectangle.
Roll up tightly into a log, left to right.
Roll the log smooth, to 12 in / 30 cm.
Cut into 8 pieces; set each on parchment.
Rise in the covered steamer, 60 min, until visibly puffed.
Fill the steamer base with water (+ vinegar), seal the lid.
Steam on high 10–12 min. Serve warm.

recipes.name: Taiwanese Popcorn Chicken
instructions: Cut chicken thigh into even 2 in / 5 cm pieces.
Mix with soy, grated ginger and garlic, white pepper, Shaoxing and egg white.
Cover and refrigerate at least 30 min.
Stir five spice, white pepper, salt and sugar together; set aside.
Dredge in sweet potato flour, packing it on — no bald spots.
Heat oil to 350°F / 175°C.
Fry 3–4 min; add basil for the last 30 sec and cover immediately.
Sprinkle the seasoning on straight out of the oil.

recipes.name: Tonkatsu (Pork Katsu)
instructions: Shred cabbage fine, slice cucumber into thin strips, toss. Chill.
Grind the sesame seeds, leaving some whole. Divide into dishes with the sauce.
Mist dried panko with water; leave 15 min to soften.
Whisk egg with oil in one tray; flour in another.
Trim fat, slit the connective tissue both sides, pound, reshape, season.
Dredge flour → egg → panko. Press panko on, rest 5–10 min.
Rest the breaded cutlets 5–10 min.
Heat oil to 340°F / 170°C, 5 cm deep.
First fry: one cutlet, 1 min per side. Rest 4 min on a rack.
Fry the second cutlet the same way while the first rests. Skim the oil between.
Second fry: raise to 355°F / 180°C, 30 sec per side each. Drain 2 min.
Slice crosswise into ¾ in / 2 cm strips. Serve with salad and dipping sauce.

recipes.name: Turnip Cake (Lo Bak Go)
instructions: Soak the dried shrimp and mushrooms in hot water, ~2 hr.
Stir-fry shrimp, mushrooms and sausage in oil 5 min; stir in scallion; remove.
Grate the daikon on the large holes of a box grater.
Simmer grated radish with 1 cup water, ~10 min, until ~1 cup liquid remains.
Whisk rice flour and cornstarch with ½ cup water.
Stir the slurry into the radish with salt, sugar and white pepper, then the filling.
Oil the pan generously; spread the batter evenly.
Steam over medium-high — 50 min loaf pan, 40 min round.
Cool and set 30 min, then turn out.
Slice ½ in / 1 cm thick with a wet knife.
Pan-fry both sides until golden and crisp. Serve with oyster sauce.

recipes.name: Yuzu Cheesecake
instructions: Line a 15 cm / 6 in pan; foil the base if it's springform.
Crush the biscuits, mix with melted butter, press into the pan.
Refrigerate the crust to set.
Heat oven to 340°F / 170°C with a deep tray inside.
Beat cream cheese, then add sugar, eggs, yogurt, flour, cream and yuzu one at a time.
Pass the batter through a sieve, then pour over the chilled crust.
Add 2 cm of 140°F / 60°C water to the hot tray; drop oven to 320°F / 160°C.
Bake 40 min at 320°F / 160°C, then foil the top and bake 15 min at 285°F / 140°C.
Turn the oven off and leave the cake inside 20 min.
Cool to room temperature, still in the pan.
Refrigerate overnight — do not unmould yet.
Unmould and slice with a knife warmed in hot water.

recipes.name: Zaru Soba (Cold Soba)
instructions: Boil sake and mirin to burn off the alcohol, then add soy sauce.
Add kombu and katsuobushi; boil, then simmer 5 min.
Off the heat, steep until cool to room temperature. Strain.
Boil unsalted water; fan the noodles in, cook 4–5 min per package.
Rinse under cold water, rubbing off the starch.
Shock in iced water 30 sec, then drain well.
Plate on bamboo mats; garnish with nori.
Dilute the concentrate with iced water; taste; divide into cups.
Chop green onions, add wasabi, serve alongside.
